</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusions</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we introduce TurboConn, a novel method that creates residual connections from higher to lower layers between sequential tokens, allowing the model’s effective reasoning depth to scale linearly with sequence length. Our results demonstrated that this architectural change yields significant performance gains on logical reasoning tasks, with only a manageable increase in computational cost. This confirms empirically that extending effective depth alone is a viable strategy for overcoming the inherent reasoning bottlenecks of fixed-depth Transformers. It would be valuable to explore the potential of this architecture further. Future work could focus on integrating this architecture into the pre-training phase, which may foster the development of more foundational, general-purpose reasoning skills.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of machine learning. There are many potential societal consequences of our work, none of which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>More Training Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Hyperparameters</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We set the learning rate for Llama 3 models to <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.92\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.92</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.92\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>. This was determined by scaling a base learning rate of <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\times 10^{-7}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times 10^{-7}</annotation></semantics></math> proportionally with our batch size of 64. For Qwen 3 models, the learning rate is set to <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.12\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.12</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.12\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8\times 10^{-8}\times 64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8\times 10^{-8}\times 64</annotation></semantics></math>. We set the decoding temperature to 1.0.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Model Implementation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement TurboConn using a cache. During the forward pass, as the model processes each token, the cache stores the hidden states from the specified higher layers. When processing subsequent tokens, these cached states are retrieved and added to the corresponding lower-layer inputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The sequential nature of TurboConn necessitates the use of a key-value (KV) cache during the training forward pass, a mechanism typically reserved only for autoregressive inference. Because tokens (or groups of tokens) are processed sequentially, the attention keys and values from all previous tokens must be cached to be available for the current token’s self-attention computation. To implement this efficiently, we store past key and value states in a list of tensors rather than concatenating them. This approach avoids the memory duplication that can occur when new tensors are created through repeated concatenation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Example Training Data</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here we offer some examples for the format of data used for training and evaluation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.1 </span>Parity</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">

<span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_rectangle" style="width:310.5pt;">
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prompt:</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">Question: Output the parity of this sequence.</span>
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.3" class="ltx_p">Input: 1 0 0 1 0 1</span>
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.4" class="ltx_p">Answer:</span>
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Completion:</span></span>

<section id="A1.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.3.2 </span>Multi-step Arithmetic</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">

<span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_rectangle" style="width:310.5pt;">
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prompt:</span></span>
<span id="A1.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_p">Question: Evaluate this expression modulo 10.</span>

<section id="A1.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">

<p id="A1.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">

<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Connection Configurations</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The downward connections are defined from a source layer to a destination layer using the notation: ‘source -&gt; destination’.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.4.1 </span>Llama 3.2 1B (16 total layers)</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A total of 15 connections were used, as specified below:</p><pre id="A1.SS4.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
6 -&gt; 0     8 -&gt; 0     8 -&gt; 2     10 -&gt; 0    10 -&gt; 2
10 -&gt; 4    12 -&gt; 0    12 -&gt; 2    12 -&gt; 4    12 -&gt; 6
14 -&gt; 0    14 -&gt; 2    14 -&gt; 4    14 -&gt; 6    14 -&gt; 8
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.4.2 </span>Llama 3.1 8B (32 total layers)</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A total of 45 connections were used, as specified below:</p><pre id="A1.SS4.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">

18 -&gt; 11   20 -&gt; 7    20 -&gt; 9    20 -&gt; 11   20 -&gt; 13
22 -&gt; 7    22 -&gt; 9    22 -&gt; 11   22 -&gt; 13   22 -&gt; 15
24 -&gt; 7    24 -&gt; 9    24 -&gt; 11   24 -&gt; 13   24 -&gt; 15
24 -&gt; 17   26 -&gt; 7    26 -&gt; 9    26 -&gt; 11   26 -&gt; 13
26 -&gt; 15   26 -&gt; 17   26 -&gt; 19   28 -&gt; 7    28 -&gt; 9
28 -&gt; 11   28 -&gt; 13   28 -&gt; 15   28 -&gt; 17   28 -&gt; 19
28 -&gt; 21   30 -&gt; 7    30 -&gt; 9    30 -&gt; 11   30 -&gt; 13
30 -&gt; 15   30 -&gt; 17   30 -&gt; 19   30 -&gt; 21   30 -&gt; 23
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A total of 21 connections were used, as specified below:</p><pre id="A1.SS4.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
12 -&gt; 4    15 -&gt; 4    15 -&gt; 7    18 -&gt; 4    18 -&gt; 7
18 -&gt; 10   21 -&gt; 4    21 -&gt; 7    21 -&gt; 10   21 -&gt; 13
24 -&gt; 4    24 -&gt; 7    24 -&gt; 10   24 -&gt; 13   24 -&gt; 16
27 -&gt; 4    27 -&gt; 7    27 -&gt; 10   27 -&gt; 13   27 -&gt; 16
27 -&gt; 19
</pre>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>LoRA Setting</h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For both 1B and 8B models we use <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=120</annotation></semantics></math> for TurboConn and <math id="A1.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=140" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>140</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=140</annotation></semantics></math> for the original model. In this section, we show that with our setup, the number of trainable parameters available to TurboConn is less than or equal to that of the standard Transformer baseline.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In both setups, LoRA was applied to several primary parameters within each Transformer block.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">There are following key dimensions:</p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{hidden}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{hidden}</annotation></semantics></math>: The hidden size of the model.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math>: The dimension of the key/value heads.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{inter}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{inter}</annotation></semantics></math>: The intermediate size of the MLP blocks.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>

<div id="A1.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">It is noted that all of these targeted modules in the base architecture are configured without bias terms.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The matrices for those parameters are unbiased. Given a LoRA rank <math id="A1.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, the total number of trainable parameters per Transformer block (<math id="A1.SS5.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{block}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{block}</annotation></semantics></math>) is calculated as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.p6" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A1.Ex9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex9X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex9X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle P_{block}=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle P_{block}=</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A1.SS5.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The total number of trainable parameters is then derived from this block-level calculation. For our method, we add the parameters from the <math id="A1.SS5.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{conn}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{conn}</annotation></semantics></math> downward connections. Each connection is a LoRA-adapted linear layer (<math id="A1.SS5.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{hidden}\to d_{hidden}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{hidden}\to d_{hidden}</annotation></semantics></math>) with an added bias. The parameter calculation is:</p>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The number of trainable LoRA parameters per Transformer block (<math id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{block}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{block}</annotation></semantics></math>), given a rank <math id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, is calculated as:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex19" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex19X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex19X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle P_{block}=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle P_{block}=</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex19X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle 4r(2048)+2r(2048+1024)+3r(2048+6144)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2048</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2048</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2048</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6144</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle 4r(2048)+2r(2048+1024)+3r(2048+6144)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex19Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex19Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle 38912r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>38912</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle 38912r</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Baseline Model (<math id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=140" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>140</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=140</annotation></semantics></math>):</p>

<p id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Our Method (<math id="A1.SS5.SSS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=120</annotation></semantics></math>):</p>

<section id="A1.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.6 </span>More Training Details for TurboConn + CoT Experiments</h3>

<div id="A1.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the original NuminaMath-CoT dataset contains a test set of only <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> problems, we perform a custom re-split of the combined training and test data to ensure more statistically stable evaluations. We randomly partitioned the dataset into <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="384,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>384,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">384,000</annotation></semantics></math> training, <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,000</annotation></semantics></math> validation, and <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,000</annotation></semantics></math> testing examples. The fixed CoT was generated by a Llama 3.2-1B model fine-tuned for <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> epochs on the original training sets, using a learning rate of <math id="A1.SS6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.4\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.4\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For GSM8K, we maintain the same experimental setup as for NuminaMath-CoT. We use the augmented GSM8K dataset described in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al. (2023)</a></cite>. However, unlike NuminaMath-CoT, GSM8K exhibits more significant overfitting to the training data; therefore, we use only 1/6 of the data to train the CoT generation model for a single epoch.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The training setup for the final prediction models remains identical to all previous experiments: we set the learning rate for Llama 3.2-1B models to <math id="A1.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.92\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.92</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.92\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, use a batch size of 64, and train for 3 epochs using all training data.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In this particular experiment, we utilized a temperature of <math id="A1.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.01</annotation></semantics></math> for evaluation to sharpen the probability distribution. This encourages the model to be more ’certain’ in its predictions, often yielding higher expected accuracy by amplifying the likelihood of the dominant choice.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</article>
